body.statement:
Fix \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\) and restrict attention to \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa,\eta}^{\mathrm{int}}\).  Under \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}primitive\text{-}clt}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}multiplier\text{-}law}\), determine whether
\[
n\kappa_n^3\to\infty,
\qquad
(n\kappa_n)^{-1/2}=o(t_n),
\qquad
t_n=o(\kappa_n)
\]
imply uniform simultaneous coverage of \([L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\) by \(\mathrm{CI}_n(t)\).  On a subclass where that implication and the hypotheses of each transferred benchmark are all valid, compare the excess width and the required margin and response-study rates of \(\mathrm{CI}_n(t)\) with (i) \(\mathrm{CI}_n^{\mathrm{proj}}\) built from an explicit simultaneous primitive region, (ii) the fixed positive random-perturbation method of Cho--Russell, and (iii) the regularized affine-projection method of Gafarov.  Determine whether the paired numerical-delta envelope has a strict width or rate advantage.  Separately, within the same response-interior subclass, fix \(\kappa_n\downarrow0\), \(n\kappa_n\to\infty\), and \(\limsup_n n\kappa_n^3<\infty\), and ask whether for every deterministic schedule \(t=(t_n)\) with \(t_n>0\) and \(t_n\to0\), there exists \(\mathbb P^{(t)}\in\mathfrak P_{\kappa,\eta}^{\mathrm{int}}\) such that \(\liminf_n\Pr_{\mathbb P^{(t)}}\{[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)\}<1-\alpha\). Require any such distortion to arise from rare-margin optimal-face switching rather than response collapse.  This is a comparison of specified procedures on their common admissible subclasses, not a minimax impossibility question.
body.justification: The remaining question is restricted to a concrete primitive response-interior subclass and compares specified procedures only where their assumptions overlap.
body.gap: Uniform face localization, critical-value validity, rare-margin sharpness, and relative width have not been derived on that repaired class.
body.consumer: A resolution would determine whether row-feasible numerical delta offers a genuine practical advantage over the honest fallback and transferred LP benchmarks.

obligation.what_is_open: On the explicitly defined response-interior subclass, prove or refute the proposed numerical-delta sufficiency window, establish or refute rare-margin face-switching sharpness, and compare excess width and rate requirements with the projected-region, Cho--Russell, and Gafarov procedures on subclasses where each method's hypotheses are jointly satisfied.
obligation.obstruction: The zero-coverage construction proves that absolute bounded-Lipschitz approximation is insufficient on the unrepaired class, but it has fixed margins and therefore says nothing about face switching. Response interiority removes that witness but does not itself establish uniform localization of nonunique primal and dual faces, relative multiplier accuracy, quantile anti-concentration, or a common rate expansion for the four procedures. Cho--Russell uses fixed positive random perturbations, while Gafarov requires uniform rank, slack, uniqueness, and moment constants that need not hold on the full shrinking-margin class.
obligation.attempted: The strengthened all-zero construction was derived with \(b_n=1/\log(n+1)\) and gives zero coverage under every schedule. A deterministic projected-region fallback was proved. The comparator LPs were then audited separately for fixed and jointly estimated costs. These steps isolate the remaining task but do not supply the new uniform face-localization or comparative-width theorem.
obligation.partial_result:
The strengthened singleton construction has fixed deployment margins, fixed response-study cell probabilities, and \(\mu_{n,cx}=2b_n/n\).  Both singleton-uniform bounded-Lipschitz discrepancies vanish, yet for every deterministic positive schedule \(t\),
\[
\Pr_{\mathbb P^0}\!\left\{[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)\right\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus fixed response interiority is one sufficient primitive restriction excluding this witness from the proposed comparison; necessity or minimality is not claimed.  Independently, the projected-region construction satisfies
\[
\{\beta_n\in\mathcal R_n\}
\subseteq
\{[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n^{\mathrm{proj}}\},
\]
so uniform primitive-region coverage supplies an honest fallback.  No theorem currently proves the proposed numerical-delta rate window, its rare-margin sharpness, or a strict width advantage on \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa,\eta}^{\mathrm{int}}\).
